chapters.title: Why it's called the Eye of Courage

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But why is this called the Eye of Courage? Aha. Because you need courage to change. You have to have it. You have to be like that tiger in the image, the first slide, Gina. Because it's a little bit uncomfortable. And then to say, this is who I am — I'm not judging myself, because that's a past seed ripening — but I have a power. I have courage. And I'm going to try to do the opposite. And slowly, over time, those limiting beliefs start turning into expansive beliefs. Slowly. You won't notice. But you'll notice one day — wow, I don't get mad at Juan anymore. I let him finish his sentence, because his heart is beautiful and he's trying to help people. And that's not about me. My anger is about me. It has nothing to do with anybody else.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But it takes courage. And you have to always have one eye on it. Please don't watch what Gina's doing — it's like the Wizard of Oz. Don't look behind the curtain. But what I'm actually saying is: do look behind your curtain. Like the Wizard of Oz, who's actually moving all the levers — that's what's going on for you, but you just had a curtain in front of it. To pull that curtain away requires a bit of chutzpah and courage.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then the cool thing that ends up happening is that leadership just happens automatically. Because you automatically become successful, because the things holding you back are no longer there. Because you're already good people. You're already helping people. Already kind. You don't have to judge yourself anymore. But we have to pull the curtain back and stop those patterns.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So there's one thing I'd like to show you before we close. Hopefully Gina got it worked out.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Most of you saw it this afternoon, earlier — not all of you. So Casa Tartuk was founded, financially, by the generous donations of Taiwan. Over 10,000 people, over the last ten years, have been supporting the growth of the Mexican branch of the V Houses — social projects, Casa Tartuk. And they are a beautiful, beautiful group. And they're studying so hard, the classic courses. The person who runs that group is Angel. Her name is Angel — kind of interesting, right? She put together this beautiful video for you last night. Did we get subtitles in Spanish, by chance?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Okay, so we're going to watch this tonight — I wanted to show it tonight just in case you don't come tomorrow. But tomorrow we're going to have a celebration here, and we're going to talk about all the cool things that Casa Tartuk has done, and the vision for the future. And I have a surprise for you too, so you should come. Please come tomorrow — it's going to be a beautiful celebration. So I want to show you this video tonight. We'll close tonight's class with it.

paragraphs.speaker: Video from Angel Chu
paragraphs.text: I'm Angel from Taiwan, representing Taiwan at the first anniversary of the opening of Casa Tartuk. The connection between Taiwan and Mexico has actually been growing for ten years. Ten years ago, Geshe Michael brought the Happy Camp mission to Taiwan. At that time, we never imagined that such a small seed could slowly connect two places so far apart. Over the ten years, more than 10,000 people have supported Happy Camp.

paragraphs.speaker: Video from Angel Chu
paragraphs.text: In July, we came to Mexico to celebrate its opening. Our Mexican friends welcomed us with so much warmth. They took us around, shared food and drinks with us, and made us feel truly at home. When we walked into the building of Casa Tartuk and saw everyone celebrating together, I was deeply moved.

paragraphs.speaker: Video from Angel Chu
paragraphs.text: During the 10th anniversary of Happy Camp last year, the Mexico team and teacher team brought ten online sessions to Taiwan, with nearly 800 people joining live online and more than 1,800 replies. And one moment I will never forget was at 6 a.m. in Mexico, when Pachi and the team gathered inside Casa Tartuk to connect with Taiwan and celebrate the 10th anniversary of Happy Camp, and to send us blessings and gratitude.

paragraphs.speaker: Video from Angel Chu
paragraphs.text: At that moment, I realized: ten years ago, we planted a seed. Ten years later, on the other side of the world, that seed has grown into a home. We are deeply grateful that Tim became our teacher in Taiwan, and grateful for our wonderful partners in Mexico, who continue to walk this path with us — learning, practicing, and growing together.

paragraphs.speaker: Video from Angel Chu
paragraphs.text: So today, on behalf of the people from Taiwan, I would like to say: Happy 1st Anniversary, Casa Tartuk! May this home hold more wisdom, more learning, and more beautiful connections. And may the story between Taiwan and Mexico continue for many more wonderful years. Thank you. Congratulations!

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I have something else to say. I know some of the people from Taiwan are on. If you can, turn on your cameras so we can see you. We had that group there, but there's a bunch of people who were able to come — some of them had other things. Actually, Angel has another nonprofit that she had a meeting for this morning, so she wasn't able to join us tonight to celebrate in person. But we just want to say, on behalf of all of us here — Angel, and everyone in Taiwan — thank you very much.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Can you put the camera on so they can see? We have a full house tonight. And that means we're going to need a bigger space soon. This is going extremely well. Thank you for your donations. Thank you for making this possible. And then tomorrow we're going to have a big celebration here. We'll talk about the future ideas. As I said, I have a surprise for you tomorrow. And I'm looking forward to seeing how this space grows — and the terrace as well. It has one of the best views in Guadalajara. I'm like, how did we land this? What seeds got planted for this amazing view? This is a premium thing to have in a big city.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So we'll talk about that tomorrow. Again, thank you, everyone in Taiwan — we're incredibly grateful for all the work you're doing. We're not broadcasting the celebration tomorrow, sorry — we don't do parties online. So, again, thank you, everyone, for joining. Thank you, tech table. Thank you to all the interpreters online. Thank you, Paola, for translating tonight.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And thank you, Aldo, for translating last night. Unfortunately, he got sick this afternoon, so he had to do dad things — his daughter — but that's life. That's committing to raising children. So thank you again, Aldo, for last night.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: We'll see you all tomorrow. And have a wonderful night. Everyone online, say goodbye to each other. Thank you.
